newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shrs end flat as investors skim off profits.
newsitem.headline: Chile shrs end flat as investors skim off profits.

text.p: Chilean shares closed flat as the market took a breather from a long buying spree, paying little heed to favorable economic data, brokers said.

The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares seesawed and finally closed 0.11 lower to 133.42 points. The general IGPA index ended 0.17 percent lower at 5726.13 points on strong volume of 186 million shares traded.

"The bolsa went up very quickly in a very short time, and what we had today was a little adjustment," said one veteran broker. "We basically had an end-of-the-year rally in June and now there's some profit-taking but I think it's still headed up."
Buy orders from U.S. institutional investors eased off a bit after a week of frenzied buying on expectations of a cut in interest rates this month or next, brokers said.

Economic figures showing a tiny 0.2 percent inflation rate in May and a slight rise in unemployment to 6.0 percent caused barely a hiccup in the market, though both numbers seemed to go in the right direction for an interest rate cut, brokers said.
"The market is still betting on a cut in interest rates, especially with inflation low," said one broker.

The next reading on the economy's performance will come on June 23, when the Central Bank issues its April economic growth figure. Growth in the first quarter was 3.4 percent, small by the standards of Chile's robust economy and contributing to expectations for a rate cut.
Gains included leading banking stocks, largely bypassed during the recent rally. Banco Edwards was up 2.8 percent to 54.50 pesos and Banco Santiago rose three percent to 10.15 pesos.

Electrical shares rose, but at a more measured pace than in the past few sessions, with Endesa up 1.6 percent at 314 pesos and Enersis up 1.7 percent at 295. Edelnor, owned by Southern Co, rose 2.9 percent to 280.
"The market was a little more selective with the electricals today," said a broker.

Decliners included Entel, off 1.8 percent to 3180 pesos after a report in the financial daily El Diario said the future of the company's planned venture into personal telephones was still unclear, and winery San Pedro, off 3.1 percent to 3.15 pesos.
